passage: I sit two seats from Kiran in the Tuesday planning meeting, so I see things. When the client's manager said the launch date would move up again, Kiran's lips pressed into a thin line and stayed there. Kiran looked at the table, nodded once, and wrote something in the notebook. Nobody else seemed to notice. I thought, either Kiran is fine with it or is choosing not to say. Honestly I cannot tell. Later in the corridor I heard Kiran tell Salma, "I should have said the timeline was not realistic. Next time I will raise it before we hang up." I only saw the pressed lips; I do not really know what Kiran was thinking. 🤔

qa.q: Where does the narrator sit in the Tuesday planning meeting?
qa.a: The narrator sits two seats from Kiran.

qa.q: What might Kiran's pressed lips have meant, and what else could they mean?
qa.a: They most likely meant Kiran was holding back a concern about the moved-up date, which Kiran later confirmed to Salma. They could also have been simple concentration, so the narrator was right not to be sure.

qa.q: What could Kiran do differently in the next meeting?
qa.a: Kiran could name the concern calmly during or right after the meeting, for example that the timeline looks unrealistic, as Kiran planned to do.

qa.q: How does Salma likely see Kiran's silence in the meeting?
qa.a: Salma probably sees Kiran as someone who thinks before speaking and wishes to speak up, since Kiran shared the regret with Salma afterwards.

grounding: Illustrates a young professional tightening lips to hold back a comment in a tense meeting, seen by an observer, with plans to name the concern later.

passage:
Week 1, Monday. In the design review, Sonali pressed her lips tight when the director dismissed her layout, said "okay", and moved on. Week 1, Thursday. Same again. Afterwards Saurabh, her desk neighbour, found her rubbing her jaw and asked if she was all right. "Fine," she said.

Week 3, Tuesday. Sonali's lips tightened again, then she breathed out and said, "Can I flag one concern about the loading time? I would like us to check it before we finalise." The director paused, then agreed to a quick test. Later she told Saurabh, "My lips give me away. Now I use that as my cue to speak, not to swallow it."

qa.q: What did Sonali ask the director to check in week 3?
qa.a: She asked to check the loading time before finalising the layout.

qa.q: Why did Sonali say "Fine" to Saurabh in week 1, and what else might her tight lips have meant?
qa.a: She was probably holding back frustration at the dismissal and did not want to discuss it yet. The tight lips could also have been plain concentration, which is why Saurabh asked instead of assuming.

qa.q: What change in approach helped Sonali between week 1 and week 3?
qa.a: She began treating her tightening lips as a signal to name the concern calmly instead of swallowing it, and the director agreed to a quick test.

qa.q: How might Saurabh have felt when Sonali said "Fine"?
qa.a: Saurabh may have felt unsure whether to press Sonali, since the answer and the rubbing of the jaw did not match, but asking still left the door open.

grounding: Illustrates a young professional pressing lips to hold back comments and later naming the concern calmly instead of swallowing it every time.
